title: Part Zero  -  The Trinity First

canonical_node.axiom: One God, three persons, one being: Father, Son, and Spirit are each fully God, yet distinct; this is the ground of all reality.
definitions: Existence: being itself; God is existence (aseity).
Distinction: real difference; Father is not Son is not Spirit.
Relation: perichoresis; mutual indwelling and lawful interaction.
Orientation: love; the mutual self-gift of the persons; the gradient of good.
Transcendentals: being, one, true, good convertible; one reality read four ways.
Divine simplicity: God does not have attributes; He is them.
derivation: Every worldview assumes existence, distinction, relation, and orientation without grounding them.
These four debts are absolved in the Trinity: existence as aseity, distinction as persons, relation as perichoresis, orientation as love.
Thus one axiom (God) replaces four unpaid assumptions.
The axiom is unprovable; its unprovability is the signature of being the ground.
The formal system can run either on the one axiom or on the four brute assumptions.
canonical_node.action: The system should treat the Trinity as the foundational axiom, deriving all subsequent ontology and ethics from it, while acknowledging the alternative of four brute assumptions.
boundary: Does not prove the existence of God; it is an axiom.
Does not derive the Trinity from prior principles.
Does not claim the fruits are derived; they are correspondences.
Does not claim the shadow is primitive; it is cast as possibility.
test: Check that all four debts (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) are explicitly absolved in the Trinity.
Verify that the axiom is not presented as proven.
Ensure that the alternative of four brute assumptions is preserved as a viable starting point.
Confirm that the fruits are labeled as correspondences, not derivations.

dg1_dependencies: Church Fathers (Gregory of Nazianzus, John of Damascus, Augustine)
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a single axiom that grounds four fundamental assumptions (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) which other systems leave unpaid.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: The four debts remain available as brute assumptions for those who reject the axiom; the formal system runs either way.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without the Trinity axiom, the framework loses its claimed ground for the four debts; it reduces to four unpaid assumptions, losing the explanatory coherence.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as axiom with explicit unprovability; do not treat as proven

overstatement_risks: Claiming the Trinity is proven rather than assumed.
Treating the fruits as derived rather than correspondences.
Implying the four debts are only payable via the Trinity.
Overstating the formalization as new math.
kill_conditions: If the axiom is presented as proven.
If the alternative of four brute assumptions is removed.
If the fruits are upgraded to derivations without evidence.
risk.lean_target: Axiom: irreducible; do not attempt to prove.

plain_summary: This document establishes the Trinity as the foundational axiom of the framework, claiming it resolves four universal assumptions (existence, distinction, relation, orientation) that other systems leave ungrounded. It explicitly acknowledges the axiom is unprovable and offers an alternative of four brute assumptions. The document is a working sheet, not doctrine, with pending items.
